own_solution.law: The long-solenoid inductance is L = μ₀N²πa²/ell = 0.00142163 H after converting lengths to metres. At steady state the winding bypasses the parallel resistor, giving I₀ = V/R₁ = 3 A. During discharge, L dI/dt + R₂I = 0, so the integrated resistor heat is LI₀²/2 = 6.39735 mJ. An aiding series emf q changes this to L[(12 + q)/4]²/2.
assumptions: Use the stated long air-cored solenoid model and negligible winding resistance.
The discharge resistor has finite positive resistance.
Use the ideal lumped circuit model in which the stored magnetic energy dissipates in the discharge resistor.

notes: All certified answers are correct in the declared target unit mJ. For aiding emfs 3.2, 7.5 and 11 V, the heats are respectively 10.2642, 16.8930 and 23.5014 mJ. Every listed positive discharge resistance cancels from the integrated heat. The torch circuit is separate, and the earlier run cannot affect the specified steady state. I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies T212D and TC1E1 as numeral-free controls, not numerical minimal pairs. The actual claimed minimal pairs, T8F98/T000E and T200B/T0F51, preserve 7.5 V and change only the intended attachment. Pass-1 answers were expressed in J; the answers here use mJ.
